todaysEvents.delta: CNBC reported Treasury Secretary Bessent unveiled 'the single greatest financial offensive ever' against Iran Monday, adding to sanctions on banking, energy, aviation and cryptocurrency, with no Chinese exemption signalled (CNBC, Aug 24).

Iran's parliament approved a provision requiring ships through Hormuz to pay for Tehran-provided services, while the PGSA warned violating vessels face fines, seizure or confiscation; Araghchi dismissed US sanctions as desperate (CNBC/Anadolu, Aug 24).

Oman's foreign minister is scheduled to visit Tehran Tuesday to continue discussions on the Strait of Hormuz joint-management arrangement, with a deal reportedly in its final stages (AP/CNBC, Aug 24).

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Oman's foreign minister visits Tehran Tuesday to discuss the joint-management plan reportedly in its final stages, but Iran's newly approved transit-fee provision and Washington's unveiled financial offensive leave a signed workable deal still required before Brent moves toward $75-85; Qatar's force majeure still limits LNG availability.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: CNBC reported the US unveiled its 'greatest financial offensive' sanctions with China not exempt, and Iran's parliament approved charging ships transiting Hormuz while the PGSA threatened seizure of rule-breaking vessels. Reduced traffic persists under a fee-and-sanctions standoff that extends into October; Brent holds $78-95 and JKM stays elevated on Qatar force majeure through mid-September.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: The PGSA warned vessels violating Iran's transit rules face fines, seizure or confiscation, and UKMTO still flags active mine danger areas; enforcement against a major tanker or a collapse of the Iran-Oman talks could renew full closure and spill into the Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb. Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu.
